business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Gibraltar (British Overseas Territory) — target commercial-registration jurisdiction; Cayman Islands (British Overseas Territory) — formation jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Common Law (English common law foundation) with offshore financial centre statutory overlay; both Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands apply English common law supplemented by their own Companies Acts, AML/CFT statutes, and BO-register decrees; the Cayman Islands is classified as a Tax_Exempt_Zone for the Exempted Company vehicle
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2019; entered into force 2020)
UK-Cayman Islands Tax Information Exchange Agreement (signed 2009; amended 2016)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to both Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands)
US-Cayman Islands FATCA Model 1 Intergovernmental Agreement (2014) — relevant for US-source payment flows via Stripe Billing and Paddle
Gibraltar-Spain Tax Agreement on Exchange of Information on Tax Matters (2019) — relevant for EU-market SaaS revenue and withholding validation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cayman Islands: Companies Act (2023 Revision); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, 2023 (in force 31 July 2024); Proceeds of Crime Act (2024 Revision); Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2024 Revision). Gibraltar: Companies Act 2014 (as amended, external companies provisions); Beneficial Ownership (Register) Act 2017; Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; Sanctions Act 2020; AML/CFT Handbook (current edition) issued by the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit (GFIU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy presented to the Gibraltar registered agent and the relevant EMI; apostille required only where the receiving bank's KYC policy expressly mandates it

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK OFSI Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Gibraltar Sanctions List (Sanctions Act 2020), and domestic PEP registers maintained by the GFIU; the no-code visual web template sector is classified as Low_Risk_Standard under both the Gibraltar AML/CFT Handbook and Cayman AML Guidance Notes; any PEP match, adverse media indicator, or high-risk residential-country nexus automatically triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD); all screening results must be archived for five years and made available for inspection by the GFIU, the Cayman AML Supervisory Authority, or the Registrar as applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands: General Registry Online Company Search and Name Reservation module (https://www.ciregistry.gov.ky) operated by the Registrar of Companies; practical filing is performed by a licensed corporate services provider. Gibraltar: Gibraltar Companies Registry e-Portal (https://www.companieshouse.gi / Registrar of Companies online services) — used for name clearance and subsequent external company registration under Form EC1.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English-only corporate naming for both jurisdictions; the legal name must appear in Latin script; any non-English trading name must be filed with a certified English translation; the Cayman Exempted Company must carry the suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; when registered as an external company in Gibraltar the identical name is retained unless the Gibraltar Registrar directs the addition of 'Cayman Islands' or a distinguishing number to avoid confusion with an existing Gibraltar legal entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Gibraltar: a rejected name may be appealed in writing to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, setting out grounds of distinctiveness and absence of confusion; if the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review within 28 days of the final decision; a reservation may be extended once for a further 30-day period upon payment of the extension fee. Cayman Islands: in parallel, a rejected Cayman name may be contested by written representation to the Registrar of Companies within 21 days, with further recourse to the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands; concurrently, the applicant should submit an alternative name to the Gibraltar Registrar to avoid losing the external-company filing window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible for the registered office of the Cayman Exempted Company; the registered office must be a physical address in the Cayman Islands maintained by a licensed corporate services provider. For the Gibraltar external-company registration, the statutory requirement is an address for service of process in Gibraltar; this may be the office of a licensed Gibraltar registered agent, which operates as a virtual service-of-process address in practice. Commercial substance must demonstrably reside in the Cayman Islands as the tax-exempt jurisdiction — the development, licensing, and operation of the no-code website builder may be managed remotely; the Gibraltar presence is limited strictly to external-company service-of-process representation and must not create a Gibraltar permanent establishment without triggering the Gibraltar 12.5% corporate income tax regime, which would undermine the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — the annualized risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection at the Cayman Islands registered office during the first 12 months is below 10% (estimated 7%); for the Gibraltar external-company service address the estimated risk is approximately 5% because the GFIU and the Gibraltar Registrar prioritize documentary UBO reporting and BO-Register accuracy over physical inspection for Low_Risk_Standard digital-service companies; nevertheless both registered offices must be physically staffed during normal business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (as amended by the Companies (Amendment) Act 2022), Part II ss. 3-21 (registration and incorporation), s. 24 (name and Certificate of Incorporation), s. 26 (registered office), s. 30 (allotment of shares), s. 31 (share capital and subscriber minimum), s. 175 (company secretary); Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) ss. 4 and 50A (qualifying-company tax-exempt status for foreign-source income).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies House Gibraltar (Office of the Registrar of Companies), 10-12 Harbours Walk, New Harbours, Gibraltar; online e-Registry portal operated under the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO1 (Application for Registration of a Private Company Limited by Shares) together with notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required by statute; nominal capital typically adopted as GBP 100 divided into 100 Ordinary Shares of GBP 1.00 each; no escrow account, capital deposit, or banker's certificate is required by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously that: (1) the subscribers shall subscribe for and take up 100 Ordinary Shares of GBP 1.00 each, fully paid, being the initial issued share capital, and the Directors are authorised to allot the same; (2) the registered office be fixed at [Address], Gibraltar, and the Registrar be directed to record the same; (3) [Name], [Name], and [Name] be appointed Director, Company Secretary, and Managing Director respectively, each to hold office until the second annual general meeting; and (4) all incorporation filings be hereby approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar - Name Reservation Unit, 10-12 Harbours Walk, New Harbours, Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies House Gibraltar e-Registry; verify that the proposed company name is not identical or deceptively similar to any name on the active register; confirm that the name ends with 'Limited' and does not contain restricted words requiring consent; submit Form ND-01 online with payment of the GBP 7.50 reservation fee; the name is then reserved for 90 calendar days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed name certificate from licensed corporate service provider
Passport copy of the initial subscriber/shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as too similar or prohibited, submit a revised name within 5 working days using the same Form ND-01; the first re-submission is exempt from an additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Notary Public (appointed by the Chief Justice) or the licensed corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English; the objects clause must cover software development, visual web-template publishing, and low-code web application building consistent with ISIC 6201; arrange for the subscriber(s) to sign before a Gibraltar notary public, who verifies identity and capacity and issues a notarial certificate of execution; prepare three sealed counterparts, one of which is delivered to the Registrar with the Form CO1 filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney if any subscriber executes by attorney
Identity documents and proof of residential address of the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defective execution (e.g., missing schedule, ambiguous witness line, uninitialed pages), the affected signature page is re-executed and re-notarized; no government fee is imposed for re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Form CO1 and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar (Companies House e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CO1 through the e-Registry portal; attach the notarized Memorandum and Articles, Form SD-1 statutory declaration of compliance, and Form RO-1 notice of registered office; pay the GBP 45 government incorporation fee; the Registrar examines the statutory objects and, if satisfied, issues the Certificate of Incorporation containing the company number and date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent-to-act forms of the sole director and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, respond via the e-Registry within 14 calendar days; if the query concerns the objects clause, file an amended memorandum approved by subscriber resolution and pay the GBP 20 amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Election of Qualifying-Company (Tax-Exempt) Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office, H.M. Government of Gibraltar (GIBTax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, notify the Income Tax Office on Form IT-101 to obtain a corporate tax reference; because the company's revenue will consist exclusively of foreign-source subscription income from no-code website builder services, submit an application for qualifying-company tax-exempt status under the Income Tax Act 2010; attach a board minute confirming the foreign-source business model, a short business plan, and a bank account introduction letter; the resultant certificate confirms 0% Gibraltar tax on non-Gibraltar derived income, subject to economic substance rules.
required_dossiers: Board minute adopting the foreign-source-only business model
Business plan and bank account introduction letter
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office requests further substance evidence, file a substance memorandum and a floor-space lease for a Gibraltar business office; any adverse determination may be appealed in writing to the Income Tax Commissioner within 30 days of the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Statutory Registers, and GDPR/VAT Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar compliance desk and Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to adopt the company seal, issue share certificates to the subscriber, and open the statutory registers of members, directors, secretaries, and charges; register for Gibraltar VAT on Form VAT-1 if taxable turnover will exceed GBP 100,000; and file a data-controller notification with the GRA under the Data Protection Act 2004 if the company processes personal data of EU or UK residents in the course of providing its low-code platform.
required_dossiers: Share certificates issued to the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual confirmation statement is rejected for incomplete registers, reconcile the registers and file a rectification notice with the Registrar within 10 working days; late-filing penalties are waived for the first inadvertent omission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) supervises electronic communications and data protection only; no industrial or sectoral operating permit is required for ISIC 6201 software publishing and low-code platform services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - the business operates under the general Certificate of Incorporation, tax registration, and, where applicable, Gibraltar VAT registration; no separate manufacturing, trade, or professional license is required for a no-code website builder.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - EIA Regulations 2000 Schedule 2 Category 4D (information technology services); no physical installation, emission point, or land disturbance, therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment or Registration Notice is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emissions; office-only sanitary wastewater as appropriate under Gibraltar Water Discharges standards (BOD 30 mg/L, TSS 50 mg/L); zero-emission computing operations; waste electronic equipment handled under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Gibraltar) Regulations 2011.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire Precautions Act 1993 (low-occupancy business premises under 60 persons, means of escape and emergency lighting inspection); Building Control structural load certificate for Class E2 business occupancy; and Occupational Safety and Health clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Cap. 197), confirming first-aid provision, electrical installation safety, and sanitary facilities at a ratio of 1 WC per 20 persons.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, Her Majesty’s Government of Gibraltar; official e-Services portal: eservices.gibraltar.gov.gi. Ancillary Cayman-side authority: Department for International Tax Cooperation, Cayman Islands (portal: ditc.ky) for CRS/FATCA and Economic Substance registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman exempted company first files an overseas-company registration with the Gibraltar Companies Registry under the Companies Act 2014 (Form OC), then submits Form A1/TFN application to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office within 30 days of acquiring a taxable presence, supported by the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, exempted-status declaration, charter documents, directors’ resolution, and Gibraltar registered-address certificate. Concurrently, the company files with the Cayman DITC its Economic Substance Notification (assessing whether website-template and low-code development services constitute a relevant activity) and its CRS/FATCA registration to obtain the Cayman TIN. The Gibraltar Tax Reference (GRN) is the operating tax ID for Gibraltar PE return filing; if central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar, the GRN attaches to a fully resident-company tax file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Cayman exempted-company status), with a Gibraltar override: upon central management-and-control or a permanent establishment in Gibraltar, the classification becomes Entity_Level_Taxation, taxing a resident company on worldwide assessable profits at 10% corporation tax, or a non-resident company with a PE on territorial profits attributable to the PE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Neither Gibraltar nor Cayman provides US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections. Gibraltar offers statutory group relief surrender elections among qualifying connected companies, unilateral or treaty double-taxation relief elections, and deductions-reallocation elections under the Income Tax Act 2010; anti-hybrid rules per OECD BEPS Action 2 are mandatory and cannot be elected away. Cayman law provides only the exempted-company undertaking declaration under section 6(1) of the Companies Law, not a flow-through tax election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar levies no VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax; the only domestic indirect impost is Gibraltar Import Duty under the Customs Tariff Ordinance, which applies to physical goods only and is outside scope for digital no-code website-builder services. EU VAT obligations may arise separately when B2C digital services are supplied to EU final consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gibraltar domestic: not applicable; no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. EU OSS (non-union seller): no de minimis threshold; mandatory registration from the first euro of B2C digital services supplied to EU consumers through the non-union OSS scheme in a chosen EU member state. B2B supplies of web-template/licensing services to EU-established recipients are reverse-charged, requiring no supplier VAT registration. Where Paddle or Stripe acts as merchant of record, the payment-platform entity assumes statutory liability for underlying VAT/sales-tax settlements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None; Gibraltar does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, SAF-T, or API-based invoicing clearance. Standard electronic invoicing (PDF, ZUGFeRD, PEPPOL) is sufficient. EU OSS filings are made quarterly through the selected EU member state’s OSS portal, reflecting aggregate cross-border B2C supplies without per-invoice fiscal authorization. The Cayman Islands impose no e-invoicing clearance regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in Gibraltar for digital services: SaaS/web-editor access, template licensing, hosting, and low-code application outputs are outside the scope of Gibraltar import duty and no Gibraltar VAT is chargeable to export. Under EU VAT rules, B2B digital supplies are reverse-charged at the customer’s location and B2C digital e-services are taxed at the customer’s member-state rate, with no 0% export rating. Physical goods may qualify for duty-free export only when leaving Gibraltar customs with evidencing movement documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (for physical goods movements only)
Commercial Invoice and service contract evidencing digital supply (subscription, template license, low-code output)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (physical shipments only)
Inward Remittance Certificate or external bank-credit settlement record evidencing FX repatriation of sales proceeds
IP/log-usage report substantiating reverse-charge treatment for B2B recipients
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar law imposes penalties under the Income Tax Act 2010 for false or misleading records: the lower of 100% of tax evaded or GBP 3,000 per return, rising with repeat defaults and criminal liability for fraudulent evasion. In the EU OSS context, misapplied 0% or incorrect member-state rate mapping is treated as VAT underdeclared, giving rise to reassessment, default interest, penalties up to 100% of the VAT due, and exclusion from the non-union OSS scheme. Misuse of dormant physical export declarations attracts customs forfeiture and civil penalties of up to three times the duty.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) in coordination with the Gibraltar Monetary Authority functions, operating under the UK Crown Dependencies framework; the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) is the relevant authority for the Cayman Exempted Company's domicile.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar uses the Gibraltar Pound (GIP) at par with GBP, and Sterling (GBP) is also legal tender and freely convertible for current and capital account transactions. The Cayman Islands use the Cayman Islands Dollar (KYD) pegged at 0.80 USD per 1 KYD, with USD accepted as customary and fully convertible. There are no exchange controls in Gibraltar or the Cayman Islands restricting current account transfers, dividend distributions, capital repatriation, or profit remittance. The corporate structure remains tax-exempt in the Cayman Islands, and Gibraltar provides a territorial tax system for non-resident controlled companies; profit remittance is freely permitted, subject to anti-money laundering (AML) source-of-funds verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Gibraltar or the Cayman Islands. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency, converted at commercial rates, or used directly for settlement, subject only to the record-keeping requirements under the Anti-Money Laundering Regulations and Economic Substance (International Tax Compliance) regulations where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for Gibraltar-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and UK-authorized EMI passported into Gibraltar, but cautious acceptance for Cayman Exempted Companies; Cayman does not issue fintech EMI licenses under a dedicated regime, so digital-only account opening is best achieved through Gibraltar-licensed fintechs (e.g., Globalise, ANNA, or equivalent) or through regulated international EMIs that accept Cayman corporate structures; legal constraint requires clear beneficial-ownership disclosure and a valid substance/economic purpose in the target market for UK or EU payment routing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for Cayman Islands account opening, but a licensed introducer of a recognized high-net-worth corporate administrator can conduct the client-onboarding interview. Gibraltar banks permit remote onboarding only where the applicant already holds a regulated financial services licence or is introduced by a GFSC-licensed corporate service provider; otherwise a physical or virtual video interview with a compliance officer is mandated for the director and controlling shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell company risk due to tax-exempt Cayman entity with no local economic substance beyond holding passive assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman Economic Substance filing, a cross-border commercial rationale memorandum, evidence of active software licence sales under ISIC 6201, corporate bank statements, and a board resolution confirming substantive business operations in Gibraltar or a trusted jurisdiction.

A full registered-owner register, nominee declaration and signed trustee acknowledgement, certified KYC of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) exceeding 25% control, and written confirmation from the Cayman registered agent that no bearer shares are issued.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth insufficiency for future high-volume transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the holding or operating entity, three months of business bank statements, executed customer contracts for the low-code web platform, tax clearance certificates, and a notarized statutory declaration of asset provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border mismatch between the Cayman legal entity and the Gibraltar operational office exposing the group to de facto permanent establishment risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A clearly executed Gibraltar substance plan, local staff payroll, office lease, board-meeting minutes held in Gibraltar, and intercompany service agreement with arm's-length pricing to neutralize PE and transfer-pricing challenges.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from UK/EU investors should be routed through SWIFT MT103 payments to a Gibraltar operational account, using purpose code 'A.01' (capital contribution) under the UK/OECD payment reporting classification and 'C.70' for software service pre-payments. Each remittance must be accompanied by a board resolution, issued-share certificate, subscription agreement, and an economy-specific source-of-funds declaration. For Cayman-side escrow funding, use SWIFT MT103 with reference 'Cayman Administrative Purpose' and make a subordinated loan or equity contribution into Gibraltar through a UK correspondent account. Verification follows the 5th Anti-Money Laundering Directive and Cayman AML Regulations; incoming digital-asset-linked funds should be explicitly rejected in the treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SaaS platform fees are settled out of the Gibraltar operating account via SWIFT MT103 corporate or commercial MT103, with purpose codes 'B.70' for software licence fees and 'B.81' for royalties, to Stripe or Paddle as the merchant-of-record trust accounts. Wholesale payments for compute, storage, and content delivery are effected by standard SWIFT MT103 or MT202, secured by commercial letters of credit (LC) where the vendor requires collateralized payment guarantees. Buyer payments for exported services may be routed through the merchant rails; the treasury function must maintain segregated ledger reconciliation between the Cayman holding company and the Gibraltar operating company. For high-value (above USD 1,000,000) software licence outflows, a SWIFT MT103 payment order plus a fully scrutinized commercial LC confirmation by a top-tier UK or Swiss correspondent bank is advised.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot GBP/USD and EUR/USD hedges executed through a Gibraltar-licensed bank or UK-authorized payment institution
Outright FX forwards up to 12 months in GBP/USD and EUR/USD booked with a prime broker or major UK clearer
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currency pairs used with clients in APAC or LATAM, only in compliance with ISDA master agreements and UK EMIR reporting
Cross-currency swaps between KYD and GBP/USD executed through a Cayman bank or global dealer, limited to treasury match-funding purposes
Zero-cost collars and participating forwards for protecting minimum SaaS revenue conversion thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Annual Return (Form B) and Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of incorporation, thereafter on each anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of USD 122 per month up to USD 610; persistent non-filing beyond 12 months triggers administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return (nil or relevant activity declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority (filed via registered office agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to USD 1,220 initial; USD 12,200 maximum and possible prosecution for continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (submitted through corporate service provider)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation (same as annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of USD 244; non-filing may result in strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Overseas Company Annual Return (required if a place of business is established in Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of overseas company registration in Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of USD 250; potential prosecution and removal from the Gibraltar register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Cayman: no statutory audit required for an exempted company without a relevant activity. Gibraltar (branch): audit required unless the company qualifies under Gibraltar Companies Act audit exemption by meeting two of three criteria (turnover ≤ GBP 10.2 million, balance sheet ≤ GBP 5.1 million, employees ≤ 50).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the company; for Gibraltar branch filings, IFRS or UK GAAP is acceptable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually confirm the accuracy of the Beneficial Ownership Register with the Cayman corporate service provider by the company's anniversary date; any shareholding transfers must be recorded in the register and reflected in the annual confirmation before filing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat rate on chargeable profits of a Gibraltar-resident company; 0% in the Cayman Islands component where the Exempted Company enjoys tax-exempt status.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: Gibraltar-source profits and foreign-source profits actually remitted to Gibraltar are chargeable, while un-remitted foreign trading income of the exempted company falls outside the charge. Gross roll-up relief and participation exemption apply to qualifying dividends and disposal gains on substantive foreign shareholdings. No capital gains tax is levied on share disposals, and no VAT or GST applies to SaaS subscription revenue. Grandfathered exempt-status offshore companies may preserve an effective 0% rate on pre-2019 ring-fenced foreign income. Practical effective rate on a pure offshore platform: 0% to 12.5% depending on situs of management, revenue, and banking.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Income Tax Return for Companies (ITO Company Return) filed with the Commissioner of Income Tax through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-Filing portal (e-services.income-tax.gi).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the end of the accounting period (for a 31 December year-end: 30 June of the following year); extensions may be granted by the Commissioner upon written application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, Gibraltar Companies House (CIGA) registration number, ELF/LEI identifier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Cayman Exempted Company trading in Gibraltar through a branch/permanent establishment must also show its branch registration number under the Gibraltar Companies Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax residence status: resident by incorporation or by central management and control (CMC) in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies only return Gibraltar-source profits attributable to a Jones-type current Gibraltar establishment; attach the CMC analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the audited financial statements of the Exempted Company; Non-UK GAAP adjustments must be reported on the reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar-source assessable trading profit (subscription and low-code platform revenue, excluding deductible expenditure).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits attributed to the Gibraltar permanent establishment should be entered; foreign SaaS receipts not remitted into Gibraltar are disclosed in the foreign-income schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income remitted into Gibraltar or received for use in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Cayman exempted company should disclaim remittance; avoid direct deposit into Gibraltar bank accounts when claiming 0% territorial treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenditure: hosting, payment-processing fees (Stripe/Paddle), development staff, legal and compliance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amortization of platform IP and intercompany charges must satisfy the arm's length standard and contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief claim: carried-forward losses within the 5-year statutory limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign losses of a Cayman head office are allowable only to the extent they are economically borne by the Gibraltar establishment.
Non-residents apply the same 12.5% rate only to PE profits; claim all deductions in the same filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Double tax relief claim under the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Gibraltar Certificate of Tax Residence and evidence of underlying foreign tax paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration: aggregate value of controlled transactions and confirmation of arm's length pricing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Cayman parent without substance must identify the UK or Gibraltar entrepreneur; disclose any intercompany IP royalty flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance declaration: relevant activity category and CIGA substance details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure holding exempted company files the reduced-substance declaration; an IP-holding platform must demonstrate employees, premises, and board meetings in Gibraltar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of GBP 100, continuing default surcharge up to GBP 60 per day (capped at GBP 3,000), and late payment interest at the statutory rate of 8% p.a. Deliberate incorrect returns attract penalties up to 100% of the tax underassessed.
